newsitem.title: FRANCE: French police crack down on illegal Asian migrants.
newsitem.headline: French police crack down on illegal Asian migrants.

text.p: French police detained 80 people on Tuesday in a crackdown on illegal immigrants from the Far East and people employing them in the garment industry, the Interior Ministry said.

The arrests in the Paris suburbs broke a ring directed by a Chinese family which specialised in smuggling illegal immigrants into France from Thailand, Laos and Cambodia and employing them in clandestine workshops, a ministry statement said.
Some 100,000 women's garments, 500 bales of cloth and some 50 sewing machines were seized during the operation, the statement said.

The operation was aimed at "breaking up illegal immigration rings and putting out of business workshops where people are employed in conditions which are an offence to human dignity," the ministry said.
Immigration is a sensitive issue in France where there are about five million foreigners, including about a million illegal immigrants, among a total population of 56 million.
The centre-right government, seeking to win back votes which in recent years went to extreme rightist Jean-Marie Le Pen's National Front party, has sought to stem illegal immigration.
Most recent illegal immigrants are from impoverished West African countries but authorities say there is also a recent sharp upturn in clandestine entries from the Far East.
